description: Consolidated inventory of remote operational surfaces. This file groups Firebase deploys, environment switching, data repair/backfill, App Check/security console work, CI gates, and App Store/TestFlight/Play release operations without changing the underlying tools.

operations.purpose: Select and verify the active Firebase/native app configuration before local builds, CI release builds, deploys, or console-driven checks, including consumer and host app roles.
requiredChecks: tool/validate_firebase_environment.sh <env> <consumer|host>
node tool/firebase/validate_google_maps_config.mjs --env <env> --platform ios
notes: Environment aliases are defined in .firebaserc.

Android flavors read apps/<role>/android/app/src/<flavor>/google-services.json, a committed link to firebase/<env>[/host]/android; the iOS/macOS build phase copies firebase/<env>[/host]/<platform>/GoogleService-Info.plist into the built app.
Only the web service worker is copied into the app project, by tool/use_firebase_environment.sh.

operations.purpose: Deploy an exact main commit's Firebase backend to dev on merge, to prod after one protected approval, and to staging monthly, in index, Functions, Firestore-rules and Storage-rules order, deploying only what changed since the environment's deployed/<env> tag.
requiredChecks: node tool/firebase/check_environment_readiness.mjs --manifest-only
node tool/firebase/check_environment_readiness.mjs --env <dev|staging|prod> --targets <csv>
node tool/firebase/check_deploy_parity.mjs --env <dev|staging|prod>
node tool/contracts/check_firestore_contract.mjs
npm --prefix functions run lint
npm --prefix functions test
firebase emulators:exec --project demo-catch-rules --only firestore,storage "npm --prefix functions run test:rules"
node tool/firebase/storage_rules_firestore_iam.mjs --all
Run node tool/firebase/probe_chat_storage_rules.mjs with an environment, user, active match, and the guarded --apply flags after Storage IAM or chat-image rules change.
notes: Delivery promotes only the impact-authorized backend subset in this order: firestore:indexes, functions, firestore:rules, storage; Hosting, Remote Config, and Extensions remain separate owning workflows or explicit operations.
The target-aware environment preflight runs before dependency installation, allows metadata-only project, secret-version, and TTL reads, forbids secret payload access, and has no apply mode.
Confirmed absence exits 1, indeterminate auth or metadata failures exit 2, and invalid invocation exits 64; every non-zero result blocks deployment.
The Storage phase fails before deploy when its Firestore Rules service-agent IAM binding is missing.
Extensions remain an explicit separate deploy path documented in docs/release_operations.md.

operations.purpose: Validate, repair, backfill, or intentionally delete Firestore data with dry-run defaults and apply guards.
requiredChecks: Prefer --json dry run before --apply.
For admin callable mutations, review the dry-run receipt and require --apply, --confirm <action-id>, and any exact --confirm-target named by the catalog.
Use --allow-prod only after reviewing prod dry-run output.
Validate a Supply Intake export without --apply, then repeat with explicit --environment, --project, and --confirm-run only to import the immutable internal shadow projection.
notes: Destructive tools require an explicit confirmation flag in addition to --apply.
Fraud/safety-related data changes should be tied back to backend_operation_catalog ownership before apply.
The Supply Intake projection importer writes only operationRuns and operationWorkItems; it cannot publish events or organizers, and a changed artifact requires a new run id.
The admin action CLI requires Firebase Auth and App Check tokens, starts a remote receipt before invoking a callable, and persists no request or response body in its receipt stores.

operations.purpose: Materialize the public organizer listing projection (website/src/generated/hostListings*.json) from one read-only snapshot of published Firestore organizers before the exact marketing build.
requiredChecks: Read Firestore only through --firestore-project; the generator never writes remote data.
Run npm --workspace catch-marketing run check:organizer-listings after materializing; both outputs must match WebsiteHostListingProjection.
Use --readiness-receipt only with --firestore-project; the receipt is evidence and cannot enable claim or review capabilities.
notes: Without --firestore-project the generator emits only demo listings; --check validates the committed outputs without network access.
Supply Intake review state stays in Operations runs, work items and Admin callables; the retired repo-backed organizer projection pipeline is not an input.

operations.purpose: Track App Check provider setup, callable enforcement, debug/release tokens, and abuse-control prerequisites that are partly managed in Firebase/GCP consoles.

entrypoints.ref: Firebase Console App Check provider registration and enforcement
entrypoints.guardrail: Record provider registration and enforcement evidence before release; no local script is allowed to claim console enforcement by itself.

entrypoints.ref: Firebase Console debug token registration for trusted devices
entrypoints.guardrail: Register debug tokens only for trusted test devices and remove stale tokens during release readiness review.

entrypoints.ref: Production admin Auth and App Check configuration
entrypoints.guardrail: After admin Auth, Hosting-domain, App Check-key, or provider changes, record console/API and live-browser evidence for authorized domains, Phone and Google providers, the App Check reCAPTCHA v3 server secret, and successful live App Check token exchange.

requiredChecks: functions/test/callable-app-check.test.cjs
tool/validate_firebase_environment.sh <env>
Console evidence for provider registration and enforcement before release or after Firebase app registration changes

For production admin changes, verify admin.catchdates.com and catchdates-admin.web.app as authorized Auth domains, the Phone provider enabled, the Google provider disabled, the deployed reCAPTCHA v3 key paired with a Firebase App Check server secret, and successful live App Check token exchange before sign-in
notes: No local script should pretend to prove console enforcement by itself.
The debug-token helper only registers an explicitly configured local token for a selected Firebase app; it does not verify provider enforcement.
The manifest makes the manual console dependency explicit for future automation.
Host Android Firebase apps were registered on 2026-06-10 and mirror the matching consumer app SHA fingerprints for dev, staging, and prod.
Host App Check provider registrations were verified in Firebase Console on 2026-06-10 for dev, staging, and prod: Android uses Play Integrity, iOS uses App Attest, and web uses reCAPTCHA Enterprise.
Firebase CLI 15.20.0 and gcloud 566.0.0 do not expose App Check app-management commands in this local toolchain.

operations.purpose: Audit every remote branch daily, report only refs with deterministic semantic-integration proof as supervised cleanup candidates, and keep stale unique-looking code visible through a failed run and maintained GitHub issue.
requiredChecks: node tool/run.mjs check git:branch-hygiene
Review the workflow artifact and prune only rows whose safeToPrune field is true.
notes: The repository delete-after-merge setting remains enabled for exact PR heads; this workflow covers squash, integration-branch, backup-ref, and no-PR visibility gaps.
The workflow has read-only contents permission and never deletes a branch.
Branches older than seven days without an open PR or semantic integration proof update one issue and fail the scheduled run.

operations.purpose: Group the CI workflows that gate contracts, Functions, Firestore rules, app builds, Admin/Marketing exact Hosting, tools, release readiness, and observability evidence.
requiredChecks: node tool/run.mjs check --manifest-only
node tool/check_remote_ops_manifest.mjs --check
notes: Workflow-specific proof still belongs in GitHub Actions run summaries.
This manifest is the local index for deciding which workflow owns which operational concern.
App Build Matrix includes host web, Android debug, and iOS simulator build coverage; Release Readiness can validate consumer, host, or both app roles.
Admin and Marketing Hosting build one production bundle, publish an immutable id/digest-bound package, and promote it without rebuilding.

operations.purpose: Build, verify and upload Consumer/Host test builds to TestFlight and the Play internal track with fastlane, and promote a tested build to production only after reviewer approval.

entrypoints.ref: App Store Connect automatic distribution to internal TestFlight groups
entrypoints.guardrail: Testers receive builds only through internal groups with automatic distribution turned on; Mobile Beta never distributes externally.

entrypoints.ref: Google Play Consumer app record and its first hand upload
entrypoints.guardrail: Consumer joins PLAY_ROLES in mobile-beta.yml only after its Play record exists and its first bundle was uploaded by hand in Play Console.

requiredChecks: node tool/run.mjs check platform:app-targets platform:verify-ios-release-identity platform:verify-android-release-identity platform:mobile-package-policy
Mobile Beta builds, verifies and uploads each build in one job from main under prod-mobile; it uploads only to TestFlight internal testing and the Play internal track.
Every beta build passes the live callable-dependency check, the iOS or Android identity verifier and the package policy before any upload.

Mobile Production runs only by manual dispatch from main in the reviewer-gated prod-mobile-release environment, and promotes an existing TestFlight build or internal-track version code without rebuilding.
notes: Build numbers come from the stores: the latest TestFlight build plus one, and the highest version code on any Play track plus one.
Each beta job records a GitHub build attestation, a job summary with the commit and SHA-256, and a 30-day artifact.

The custom Mobile Internal Release and Promote pipeline was retired after Mobile Beta run 40975670519 uploaded both iOS apps to TestFlight and run 40943509998 uploaded Host Android to Play internal; see docs/plans/mobile_release_fastlane_migration.md.
Apple Developer App ID Catch Host/com.catchdates.host and App Store Connect app id 6778927317 were created on 2026-06-10; SKU is catch-host-ios.
App Store Connect displays an updated Apple Developer Program License Agreement notice that the Account Holder should accept before treating host uploads/submissions as release-ready.
App Store review metadata and TestFlight group membership remain console-owned.

operations.purpose: Reserve, verify, provision and activate an exact client form subdomain, or revoke routing and remove exact origin grants, through a trusted read-only-default operator.
requiredChecks: node tool/run.mjs check firebase:form-domain-operator
Build the exact reviewed Functions source before invoking the operator.
Review the default read-only dry run with exact environment, organizer, form, manager UID and reservation generation before --apply; production also requires --allow-prod.
Verify actual deployed website, Hosting TLS, DNS, App Check, upload and submission behavior on the client domain before onboarding acceptance.
notes: No client domain or provider activation is required to publish source.
ADC authenticates the operator independently of the requesting manager UID; current manager and exact reservation authority are rechecked.
Serialize operator and console edits to shared Auth and Enterprise configuration; only bucket CORS supports a metageneration precondition.
Rollback revokes registry routing before removing exact grants; inherited parent domains and wildcard CORS remain explicit residual trust. Hosting deletion and DNS changes are separate operations.
